This case having been heard and served for orders, com  pronouncement this day, the court pronounced the following:

ORDER Petitioner has filed this petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India making a prayer to quash order dated 19.11.2022 contained in Annexure-P/8 and prayer was made for direction to constitute State Level Enquiry Committee in accordance with letter dated 09.08.2021 contained in Annexure-P/5.
Later on, petitioner has filed an application for proposed amendment, which was allowed.

Petitioner made further prayer for quashing of FIR in connection with Crime No.612/2022 registered at Police Station-Lalbagh District-Burhanpur against the petitioner.
2 . Annexure-P/8 dated 19.11.2022 is a letter written by Assistant Commissioner representing Collector District-Burhanpur to In-charge Police Station-Lalbagh District-Burhanpur.

Letter was written to In-charge Police Station on basis of complaint made by one Suryakant @ Anand Dixit and Collector had constituted enquiry Committee which had submitted it's report dated 15.11.2019, on basis of which, Assistant Commissioner has written impugned letter dated 19.11.2022 for registration of FIR.
As per said report, various bank accounts were opened contrary to instructions of Govt. of MP.
Government money was deposited in said accounts.
Later it was withdrawn without any need.
Directions issued by State Govt. for e-payment was also violated.

In complaint of Dr.
Suryakant @ Anand Dixit, it was alleged that in account of Swati Mukesh and Pallavi Balkrishna, an amount of Rs.10,07,500/- was credited but no accounts or documents were maintained regarding said payments.
Irregularity was committed between 25.06.2010 to 20.06.2017.

At the relevant time,
petitioner namely Narayan Patil was Assistant Grade-III and he w a s conducting the work of accounts department.
From A/c No.026721100000336, illegal withdrawal and disbursement was made.
Petitioner was having suspicious role in transactions and request was made for registration of FIR against him.

3. Petitioner has challenged impugned actions of respondents and letters on grounds that letter dated 19.11.2022 was written without application of mind and without considering report of Special Enquiry Committee.

It is submitted that first report of Local Enquiry Committee dated 04.10.2019 lost it's utility as subsequent report of Special Enquiry Committee dated 02.12.2019 held that petitioner was made a scapegoat on the basis of old and stale report.
Entire amount, which was transferred in account of persons, has been returned by them.

By filing rejoinder, counsel appearing for petitioner brought facts on record that respondent No.6-Shri Baliram Dhurve has filed W.P.
No.3328/2023 challenging enquiry report dated 02.12.2019.
Respondent No.6 deliberately concealed the aforesaid report in W.P. No.23636/2023.

sentences.text: Collector-Burhanpur was directed to file affidavit with regard to progress and investigation and action taken against delinquent employee.

In pursuance to order dated 17.11.2022,
Collector-Burhanpur lodged complaint dated 19.11.2022 at Police Station-Lalbagh District-Burhanpur.
After lodging of FIR, W.P. No. 23636/2023 was withdrawn.
Respondent No.6 has misconducted himself by suppressing the facts from Court and also committed civil contempt.
In these circumstances, counsel appearing for petitioner made a prayer for quashing of impugned orders and also to initiate proceedings against Respondent No.6.-Baliram Dhurve.
4 . Counsel appearing for the respondent No. 6 raised preliminary objection regarding maintainability of writ petition for quashing of FIR.
It is submitted that petitioner is having alternate remedy and therefore, writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not maintainable.
It is also submitted that incorrect statements were made by petitioner.
No facts were suppressed in W.P. No. 23636/2022.

Since FIR has been registered against petitioner, therefore,
writ petition filed by petitioner has become infructuous.
Action has already been taken against him and liberty was sought to file fresh petition if grievance remains unaddressed.

Further delinquent officer has done embezzlement and in collusion with higher authorities, second report was prepared,
which is favourable to petitioner.
It is submitted that departmental enquiry was conducted against petitioner and after enquiry, punishment order of dismissal from service was passed on 05.08.2019 and same has not been disclosed.
On basis of aforesaid submissions, prayer was made for dismissal of writ petition.
5. Government Advocate appearing for State submitted that there are two enquiry reports; in one report, a financial irregularity is found while other report absolved petitioner.

Respondent No. 4 on basis of earlier communication and variations reflected in enquiry report has submitted a complaint before respondent No. 5 i.e. Station House Officer, Police Station Lalbagh, District Burhanpur,
wherein embezzlement of Rs. 10,27,36,969/- was found.

entities.text: Station House Officer, Police Station Lalbagh, District Burhanpur
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Prima facie case for offence under Sections 420 and 409 of Indian Penal Code is made out against petitioner.
Though, recommendation was made by Collector for constituting State Level Enquiry Committee about the variation in two reports but, said enquiry is not necessary.
Respondent No. 5 will consider the reports and proceed on basis of its own investigation and if there is no material against petitioner, then he may be acquitted in the case.
Respondent No. 5 is an appropriate authority to investigate the offence.
It is further submitted that there is no bar in proceeding parallelly in departmental enquiry and criminal investigation.
Action initiated by respondent by lodging FIR is just and proper.
In view of same, writ petition filed by petitioner be dismissed.

6. Heard the counsel for the parties.
7 .
First Information Report is only an information to police regarding commission of a cognizable offence.
Said information can be given orally or in writing to officer incharge of police station.
Such information does not decide the guilt of the a person.
Information only sets wheels of criminal investigation in motion.
After lodging of FIR, police starts investigation in the case.
If in investigation, it is found that offence is made out, then final charge-sheet is filed before the Court and if it is found that offence has not been committed, then closure report is filed.
Accused gets a right to defend himself in Court against allegations which are made in final charge-sheet.

sentences.text: Now investigation will be done by police on their own and they will collect the evidence on record and thereafter, final report will be filed.
Lodging of FIR against a person is only an information for conducting investigation.
Whether petitioner has committed offence or not is to be seen by investigating agency.
Second enquiry report has given clean chit to petitioner, is not a ground for quashing of FIR.

Second enquiry report has absolved petitioner but, investigating agency has to satisfy itself whether any cognizable offence has been committed or not and file charge-sheet under Section 173 Cr.P.C. or file a closure report.
8. Complaint was lodged at Police Station Lalbagh, District Burhanpur against petitioner.
Police Station has registered offences against petitioner on basis of information received by it.

Prima facie,
there appears to be material in FIR that petitioner has committed cognizable offence.
He may have been subsequently absolved by second enquiry committee but investigating authority has right to proceed with investigation and reach its own conclusion.
In view of same, no interference is called for and FIR cannot be quashed.
9. Counsel appearing for the petitioner further submitted that respondent No.6 has suppressed the fact of Second Enquiry Committee report from Court to get a particular order from Court.

On going through order dated 02.12.2022 passed in W.P. No. 23636/2022, it is found that petitioner therein namely Baliram Dhurvey has withdrawn writ petition as FIR has been registered against Narayan Patil.
While withdrawing petition, petitioner Baliram Dhurvey was granted liberty to assail enquiry report if he is so advised.

After dismissal of W.P. No. 23636/2022, respondent No.6 namely Baliram Dhurvey has filed petition on 04.02.2023 challenging second enquiry report, in which petitioner namely Narayan Patil was absolved.
This shows that respondent No. 6 was not having any malafides and he has challenged subsequent enquiry report by filing writ petition before this Court.
In view of same, no action is required to be taken against respondent No.6 namely Baliram Dhurvey.

10. Writ petition filed by petitioner is dismissed.
